name: video-preview-enhanced
description: Play MP4, MKV, MOV, AVI and WebM with sound in VS Code. Remote-SSH, WSL, video URLs, frame-accurate stepping, synchronized comparison and PNG export.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode only the built-in (sandboxed WebAssembly) decoder runs; native ffmpeg never does.

videoPreviewEnhanced.autoplay.description: Start playing when a video opens.

videoPreviewEnhanced.advancedMode.description: No longer used: the player has one layout, and its tools (compare, scopes, inspector, stats, X-ray, A-B export) are always in the player's settings panel (the cog).
videoPreviewEnhanced.advancedMode.deprecationMessage: No longer used: the tools are always in the player's settings panel (cog).

videoPreviewEnhanced.jump.arrow.markdownDescription: How far **Left** / **Right** jump in the player: `"frame"` is one frame, a number is seconds. **,** and **.** always step one frame. Set it here in VS Code's Settings (the player's ⚙ menu has no page for it).

videoPreviewEnhanced.jump.shift.markdownDescription: How far **Shift+Left** / **Shift+Right** jump in the player: `"frame"` is one frame, a number is seconds. **,** and **.** always step one frame. Set it here in VS Code's Settings (the player's ⚙ menu has no page for it).

videoPreviewEnhanced.jump.ctrl.markdownDescription: How far **Ctrl+Left** / **Ctrl+Right** (**Cmd** on macOS) jump in the player: `"frame"` is one frame, a number is seconds. **,** and **.** always step one frame. Set it here in VS Code's Settings (the player's ⚙ menu has no page for it).

videoPreviewEnhanced.jump.wheel.markdownDescription: How far the **scroll wheel** jumps while the video is paused: `"frame"` is one frame, a number is seconds. **Ctrl+wheel** still zooms.

videoPreviewEnhanced.jump.wheelShift.markdownDescription: How far **Shift+wheel** jumps while the video is paused: `"frame"` is one frame, a number is seconds.

videoPreviewEnhanced.stepButtons.markdownDescription: What the two buttons beside Play do in the player. `"frame"` (default): step one frame back / forward. `"jump"`: jump back / forward by the **Ctrl+Left** / **Ctrl+Right** size (`jump.ctrl`, 1 frame or 1-30 s). **,** and **.** always step one frame. Set it here in VS Code's Settings (the player's ⚙ menu has no page for it).

enumDescriptions: The whole picture is visible; bars where its shape differs from the player's.
No bars: the picture covers the player and its edges are cropped, centred.
The picture fills the player and is distorted to do it.
One video pixel is one screen pixel; drag to move a picture larger than the player.
videoPreviewEnhanced.pictureSize.markdownDescription: How the picture sits in the player for **new** tabs, in the player and in compare: `"fit"`, `"fill"`, `"stretch"` or `"actual"` (100 %). The button beside the keyboard shortcuts and the **Z** key change the current tab only.

videoPreviewEnhanced.compare.openTogethe.markdownDescription: Videos that VS Code opens together (several files selected in the Explorer, then **Open With…**, Enter or double-click) open in **one compare view** instead of separate tabs. Opening one video, or videos a moment apart, is not affected. Up to `compare.maxVideos`.

videoPreviewEnhanced.compare.maxVideos.markdownDescription: How many videos one compare view takes (2–16). From 5 videos on they are shown in a static grid (3×2, 3×3, 4×3, 4×4) and share the memory and transfer budgets of 4, so each picture gets fewer pixels. Applies to the next compare you open or a video you add.

enumDescriptions: Native ffmpeg when it is installed, for everything except 8-bit H.264 and VP8 (those play on VS Code's GPU decoder), in local and WSL windows. Otherwise, and over SSH or in containers, the built-in decoder. Pixel tools can switch a tab to the built-in decoder for exact pixels.
Always the built-in decoder (WebAssembly + the GPU decoder in VS Code).
Always native ffmpeg when it is installed (local windows and WSL).

videoPreviewEnhanced.ffmpegPath.description: Path to your own ffmpeg for native decoding. Empty: the one setup downloaded, then PATH.

videoPreviewEnhanced.gpuDecoding.description: Let native ffmpeg decode on the GPU, with the method the ffmpeg test found best on this machine (d3d11va, qsv, cuda, dxva2, vaapi, videotoolbox). Off: CPU decoding only, and the test tries no GPU method.

enumDescriptions: HDR10 (PQ) and HLG video is shown in HDR when the display reports HDR (Windows: "Use HDR" on), else tone-mapped to SDR.
Always tone-map HDR video to SDR.
videoPreviewEnhanced.hdrOutput.description: How HDR video (HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision profile 8, HDR10+) is shown.

videoPreviewEnhanced.nativeMaxHeight.description: Native decoding scales larger videos down to this height for display. 0 (automatic): in a local window raw frames reach the editor through a private local connection (127.0.0.1, this window only), and videos play at full resolution up to 2160p when their frame rate allows (4K at 30 fps in full, 4K at 60 fps at 1440p); when that connection is unavailable, and in WSL, frames go through VS Code's messages at 1080p (720p in WSL). A number: that height, whichever way the frames go.

videoPreviewEnhanced.sizeFramesToView.markdownDescription: Performance: with ffmpeg, send frames only as large as the picture is shown (540p to 2160p), which saves a lot of CPU for 4K videos. The picture grows to full resolution at once when you enlarge the panel, go fullscreen or zoom in. Turn off to always get frames up to `#videoPreviewEnhanced.nativeMaxHeight#` (automatic: 2160p for 4K at 30 fps). A number in `nativeMaxHeight` wins either way.

enumDescriptions: Automatically use Live transcode when needed (over remote links, or locally when raw frame transfer falls behind).
Always start with Live transcode for non-HDR files that qualify (avoids startup stutter on 4K60 or fluctuating SSH links).
videoPreviewEnhanced.transcode.markdownDescription: Live transcode (ADR 0002): let ffmpeg on this host (local or remote) transcode video on the fly to a low-latency H.264 stream for WebCodecs. Prefers GPU decode and GPU encode when available, with software encoding as the last resort. **Copy Frame**, **Save Frame**, **Pixel Inspector** and **Scopes** automatically fetch full-resolution source frames when available. Pixel Inspector and Scopes fetch them while paused. 100% live zoom uses the playback picture. Changes in ⚙ › Live transcode set the default for all videos on this machine and can reload the current tab.

videoPreviewEnhanced.transcodeMaxBitrate.markdownDescription: Maximum bitrate in Mb/s for Live transcode (`0` = Auto; non-zero values are clamped to at least `0.25` Mb/s / 250 kb/s). Uses best quality capped strictly at this ceiling (capped VBR) so the stream never exceeds your link budget while staying compact on easy or low-fps scenes. Also set in ⚙ › Live transcode.

videoPreviewEnhanced.transcodeSplitBitra.description: Share an explicit Live transcode max video bitrate across Compare tiles using Live transcode. Each tile has a 250 kb/s minimum. Auto budgets each tile by its size and frame rate.

videoPreviewEnhanced.remoteStream.deprecationMessage: Replaced by videoPreviewEnhanced.transcode (auto -> auto, off -> off, on -> always).
enumDescriptions: In remote windows (SSH, WSL, containers, tunnels), formats VS Code's GPU decoder can't play (anything but 8-bit H.264 and VP8) are re-encoded by ffmpeg on the remote machine as a low-latency H.264 stream, when native ffmpeg can't play them there directly (it does in WSL). Needs ffmpeg on the remote machine; uses its GPU encoder (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF, VAAPI) when it has one.
Disable remote H.264 re-encoding. Normal decoder selection still applies.
In every window, local ones too (for testing).
videoPreviewEnhanced.remoteStream.markdownDescription: Deprecated: use `#videoPreviewEnhanced.transcode#` instead. Kept for backwards compatibility.

videoPreviewEnhanced.fastPreviewWhenBehi.description: Built-in decoder, HEVC and H.264 only: while playback is behind real time, leave out deblocking for about 1.2-1.5x faster decoding. The picture is approximate while playing; paused and stepped frames are always decoded exactly.

videoPreviewEnhanced.overrideFileIcons.markdownDescription:
Override the file icon of every video format the player opens (such as `.mkv`, `.flv`, `.m2ts`) with the video icon VS Code's default Seti theme uses for `.avi` and `.mov`. It adds `"*.ext": "vpe-video"` entries to your user `files.associations`, only where you have none; turning it off removes just those.

Why the extension starts with VS Code: so the icons (and the one-time default-viewer setup) are in place before you open your first video. Loading takes about 30 ms per window (Extensions view, Running). VS Code doesn't let a setting change when an extension loads, so it still loads with this off, but then it does no file-icon work.

enumDescriptions: Show every frame: playback slows down to the decoding speed (sound pauses while behind). Reliable when decode times vary.
Keep real time: jump to the next keyframe when behind. Choppy; falls back to every frame when decoding is far too slow.
videoPreviewEnhanced.whenSlow.description: What to do when a video decodes slower than real time. The slow-playback notice can switch it for you.
